Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0004", "row_sha256": "0613303577c3b7e2b500b58557a7798af739322d88ae6f977027a801adea47e8", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need a prompt for a good set of instructions for Orson, not Nadia, about making one desktop shortcut on our laptop. it's Linux Mint 22 with Cinnamon and the account name is mira. Xed is already installed and the note is already there at /home/mira/Projects/harbor/weekly-log.md. the point is that when Orson uses the shortcut from the desktop, it should open that note directly in Xed. i don't want a general app launcher or a shortcut that just opens the Projects folder. the note name and path are correct, and the file exists, so don't make the guide start by searching for it or creating a new file.

Orson told me, "I want to get straight to the weekly log, not hunt through folders every morning." The desktop item can be called Weekly log. It should be put on the Desktop and use a suitable ordinary text-file icon if Cinnamon supplies one; we aren't asking for a custom picture or a special design. The result needs to be a normal desktop shortcut that a person can use, not a note explaining what a shortcut is. I haven't tried making one yet. Please don't imply that I have already opened a launcher editor or changed any permissions.

The reader is comfortable clicking around but doesn't know Linux launcher details. Explain the graphical way first, with steps in the order Orson should do them and the Cinnamon labels where you know them. I would rather not use a terminal. There are already enough ways to get lost in instructions, so please don't mix a terminal command into every step or make the first option depend on typing commands. If Cinnamon's graphical route isn't available on this setup, include a small terminal fallback as a separate alternative, not as the normal route. Say clearly which route is the fallback. Don't pretend a menu item has a particular label if the label can vary by Cinnamon version.

1. what it should do: launch the exact file `/home/mira/Projects/harbor/weekly-log.md` in Xed, not launch Xed with an empty document, and not open the containing folder in the file manager. Keep the note where it is. The name of the desktop shortcut should be Weekly log, even though the actual file is called weekly-log.md. Don't suggest renaming the note to match the shortcut. I don't need instructions for making similar shortcuts for other documents.

Please make the permission part understandable, because I've heard desktop launchers can need to be trusted or marked executable. Explain only the permission or trust step that's relevant to using a desktop launcher on this Cinnamon desktop. Make clear that this is not a shell script and that nobody should run the markdown note as a program. If Cinnamon shows a first-use trust or confirmation prompt, explain what Orson should check before accepting it; if it doesn't show one, don't invent an error or say that it definitely will. Don't ask for an administrator password, don't install software, and don't change system-wide settings. The Xed app is already present.

For the main route, have the guide say how to create or save the launcher on the Desktop, set its displayed name, and set the command or target so it opens the note in Xed. Use the exact path above in the prompt you write, and take care not to lose the `.md` ending or change the capitalization. The path doesn't contain spaces. If the launcher editor asks for a name, command, comment, or icon, explain which fields matter for this task and which can be left alone; don't make up an icon file path. The shortcut should point to the existing document rather than copy its contents into a launcher field. If some details depend on how the Mint menu is worded, say that briefly and give Orson enough clues to identify the right control without claiming we've checked his screen.

Please keep the eventual instructions practical, plain English, and not too technical, but include enough detail that a beginner can follow them without guessing what to click next. A short numbered sequence makes sense. Separate the graphical steps from the fallback, and don't give two competing procedures in the same numbered step. If the fallback is needed, keep it minimal and explain what it changes on the Desktop; don't include a script, package installation, or unrelated shell tutorial. Do not perform the setup in your answer; I need a prompt that requests the guide, not the guide itself.

The guide should finish with a simple check Orson can do: use the new Desktop item and confirm that the existing weekly log opens in Xed. If it opens a different file, an empty Xed window, or the folder instead, the instructions should tell him which launcher detail to recheck, without claiming that any of those outcomes has happened. He should be able to keep editing and saving the original note at its existing location. Don't ask him to make a backup, alter the note's contents, or rearrange the Projects folders. For this request the endpoint is just this one working desktop shortcut; nothing about scheduling, syncing, sharing, or changing the laptop's broader setup is needed.", "output": "Write a practical, beginner-friendly guide for Orson, not Nadia, to create one desktop shortcut on a laptop running Linux Mint 22 with Cinnamon. The account name is `mira`. Xed is installed, and the existing note is `/home/mira/Projects/harbor/weekly-log.md`. The shortcut should be placed on the Desktop, be displayed as “Weekly log,” and open that exact note directly in Xed. It should not open an empty Xed document or the containing folder, and it should not be a general app launcher. The note already exists and must remain at its current location.

Orson said, “I want to get straight to the weekly log, not hunt through folders every morning.” He can use a graphical interface but is unfamiliar with Linux launcher details. Give the graphical method first, with steps in order and Cinnamon control names where known. Menu wording may vary, so explain how to recognize the relevant control rather than claiming a particular label is present. If the graphical method is unavailable, provide a clearly separate, minimal terminal fallback; do not make terminal use the standard route or mix commands into the graphical steps.

Use a short numbered sequence for the main procedure. Explain how to create or save the launcher on the Desktop, set its displayed name to `Weekly log`, and set its command or target to open `/home/mira/Projects/harbor/weekly-log.md` in Xed. Preserve the exact path, capitalization, and `.md` extension. If the launcher editor includes fields for a name, command, comment, or icon, identify which fields matter and which can be left blank or unchanged. Do not invent an icon-file path; an ordinary text-file icon supplied by Cinnamon is suitable. The path contains no spaces. The shortcut must point to the existing note, not copy its contents into a launcher field. Orson has not yet tried to make the launcher or change permissions, so do not imply otherwise.

Explain only the permission or trust step relevant to using a desktop launcher in this Cinnamon setup. Make clear that the launcher is not a shell script and the Markdown note must not be run as a program. If Cinnamon displays a first-use trust or confirmation prompt, explain what Orson should check before accepting it; do not assert that such a prompt will definitely appear or invent an error. Do not require an administrator password, software installation, or system-wide settings changes. The fallback, if needed, should briefly explain what it changes on the Desktop, and must not include a script, package installation, or unrelated shell tutorial.

Keep the guide practical, plain-English, and detailed enough that a beginner can follow the steps without guessing. Do not provide competing procedures within the same numbered step. End with a simple check: Orson should use the new Desktop shortcut and confirm that the existing weekly log opens in Xed. If it instead opens another file, an empty Xed window, or the folder, explain which launcher detail to recheck without suggesting that any such problem has already occurred. The note should remain editable and saveable at its existing location. Do not instruct Orson to alter its contents, rename it, make a backup, or rearrange the Projects folders. Keep the request limited to this one desktop shortcut; do not cover scheduling, syncing, sharing, or broader laptop setup. Provide the guide, not instructions for making a prompt or performing unrelated tasks."}]
